reason: Adding falling dust to the young star's disk seems a useful starting point for gathering pebbles.
expectation: The dust will join or settle into the disk, perhaps preparing grains to stick together.

alternatives.reason: The warm inner disk also relates to rocky material, but I want to follow the incoming dust first.

effect: The dust has settled into the disk, making slowly meeting grains a plausible next step toward pebbles.
reaction: The role of gas drag in concentrating the dust was interesting.
reason: Slow collisions seem more likely to let grains stick together than break apart.
expectation: The settled dust and slowly meeting grains may form larger aggregates, though they might not yet be pebbles.

alternatives.reason: The inward-moving icy grains might also contribute rocky material, but I want to follow the settled dust first.

effect: Gentle collisions produced fragile clumps, suggesting that fast grains could test what a hard collision leaves.
reaction: The contrast between gentle sticking and possible breakup is interesting.
reason: Combining the fragile clumps with fast grains directly addresses the hard-collision goal.
expectation: The fast encounter may break the clumps into smaller fragments rather than build pebbles.

alternatives.reason: The warm disk may help produce rocky material, but I want to test the clumps first.

effect: The hard collision shattered the clumps and completed that goal; gathering rocky pebbles remains.
reaction: The breakup was expected, but the reversal of earlier growth was satisfying.
reason: The warm inner disk may remove ice from the inward-moving grains, helping gather rocky material.
expectation: The ice may evaporate in the warm disk, leaving rocky grains or pebbles.

alternatives.reason: The shattered grains might stick together again, but the warm disk seems more directly relevant to the remaining goal.

effect: The ice evaporated, leaving rocky grains that can now meet slowly.
reaction: The clarification that the ice changes phase rather than vanishes was useful.
reason: Slow encounters may let the newly exposed rocky grains stick together toward the remaining pebble goal.
expectation: The rocky grains may form larger clumps or pebbles through gentle collisions.

alternatives.reason: The shattered grains could also regrow, but the ice-stripped grains connect more directly to rocky pebbles in the warm disk.

effect: Gentle encounters formed rocky pebbles and completed the remaining goal; the result also made clear that sticking alone is not enough to make planets.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the rocky grains become pebbles, with a useful qualification about their limits.

mostWorthwhile.text: Breaking the fluffy clumps with fast grains made the contrast between growth and fragmentation tangible.

leastWorthwhile.text: Settling the incoming dust was a straightforward setup step, though the explanation of gas drag gave it some interest.

surprise.text: The pebbles result clarified that further sticking alone cannot take them all the way to planets.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless; the offered compatible choices and their results gave each a clear role.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see what processes bridge the gap between pebbles and larger bodies, especially after the ending qualified what sticking can accomplish.
